correctness.rationale: Full 32767-mask enumeration and an independent forbidden-triple face predicate agree on exactly 746 nonempty faces; lexicographic pivot matching produces 370 pairs and one critical 0-cell plus five critical 3-cells. Direct topological sorting exhaustively certifies absence of cycles in the 2580-cover directed Hasse graph; Forman discrete Morse theory yields exactly a wedge of five S3 integrally. Independent mod-two boundary rank checks corroborate but do not substitute for the homotopy argument.

originality.rationale: The exact degree-at-most-one/P3-free complex on KG(6,2) was compared by implications with published primary results, indexed scientific records for the same graph, alternative terminology and a full own-ledger claim scan. Taylan treats other graph classes, Braun and Feng–Wang treat ordinary independence, Chau et al. treat asymptotic extremal degree; the closest indexed KG(6,2) results treat Čech and neighborhood complexes. No checked statement entails the integral five-three-sphere wedge. Unindexed priority risk persists.

value.rationale: KG(6,2) is the smallest member of the canonical two-subset Kneser family admitting three pairwise disjoint pairs, hence triangles. Its P3-devoid complex is a natural first triangle-bearing boundary case beyond the Petersen graph. A complete integral five-three-sphere homotopy classification, not inferable from known ordinary independence results or mere Betti numbers, is a reusable exact benchmark for higher Kneser-independence complexes. No unproved broader downstream theorem is asserted.
